# Vinyl player
**A cartoon turntable for Bilibili audio, living inside the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI.**
Search for music · drop a record on the platter · keep listening while you work
## What it is

A record player, not a music app. There is no list of files, no playlist sidebar,
no transport bar f

ull of buttons — there is a **turntable**. You search for a song,
a record appears in a crate, you d
rag that record onto the platter, and it plays.

The whole panel is drawn as an illustration: a wooden cabinet, a spinning black
disc with a paper la

bel, a chrome tonearm, a speed selector and a volume knob. It
is meant to feel like a small object s
itting on your desk rather than another tab.

And because the audio lives outside the panel, **you can close the panel and the
music keeps playing
** while you work elsewhere in the app.
## The panel

| Turntable | Records |
| :--: | :--: |
*Left: the deck itself. Right: how the panel is arranged.*
The deck is the centre of the panel. Underneath it sit two shelves:

- the **record crate** — whatever your last search turned up
- the **favourites shelf** — the record

cord crate** — whatever your last search turned up
- the **favourites shelf** — the records you kept

Hover a sleeve and it swells toward you. Drag it onto the platter and it plays.
Drag it onto the fav
ourites shelf and it is collected.
## The tonearm is the transport

There is no play button on the deck. To play, **drag the tonearm onto the record**.
To pause, **lift

it back onto its rest**. The arm follows your pointer around its
pivot, and it works from the keybo

onto its rest**. The arm follows your pointer around its
pivot, and it works from the keyboard too.

This is the whole interaction, and it is why the panel has no transport bar: the
gesture that starts
the music is the gesture a real turntable uses.

Secondary controls — previous, stop, replay, next — sit underneath, along with a
progress bar you ca

n drag. The grey band ahead of the thumb shows how much of the
track is already buffered.
## Features
| **A drawn, not assembled, interface** | Every part of the deck is vector artwork: gradients for th

e brushed metal and the vinyl sheen, a real paper label, a perspective-free front view. |
| **Drag a

s the only verb** | Drag to play, drag to collect, drag to scrub. No settings panel, no menus. |
| *
*Playback that outlives the panel** | Close the panel, keep the music. The sidebar entry keeps the c

urrent record in view. |
| **A crate and a shelf** | Search results become sleeves; the ones you kee

p get their own shelf and survive a reload. |
| **Honest buffering** | The progress bar shows played

, buffered, and not-yet-loaded as three separate bands. |
| **Both languages** | English and 简体中文, f

ollowing the app's locale. |
| **Nothing written to disk** | Audio is streamed and released the mome
nt you change track. |

### Afterwards

Reload the Web GUI. A **黑胶唱片机 / Vinyl player** entry appears in the sidebar;
open it and you have a

Web GUI. A **黑胶唱片机 / Vinyl player** entry appears in the sidebar;
open it and you have a turntable.

Requirements: a DeepSeek Harness Web GUI profile, and a network path to
`bilibili.com`. Node 20+ is
only needed to run the tests.

Installing into a profile affects every session in that profile, and the plugin
survives a restart.
## Using it
| Do this | And this happens |

| Type in the search box | The crate fills with records |
| Click a sleeve | It plays |
| Drag a sle

eve onto the platter | It plays |
| Drag a sleeve onto the favourites shelf | It is collected, witho

ut playing |
| Drag the tonearm onto the record | Play |
| Drag the tonearm back to its rest | Pause

|
| Drag the progress bar | Scrub through the track |
| Click the heart on a sleeve | Keep it, or l

the progress bar | Scrub through the track |
| Click the heart on a sleeve | Keep it, or let it go |
## How it fits together

The bundle has two halves, and they exist because a browser cannot talk to
Bilibili directly.

**The host half** does the talking: it obtains an anonymous visitor cookie, signs
its requests, and

exposes four endpoints the panel can call — search, resolve a
video's track list, resolve a playable

stream, and proxy artwork. Audio itself is
proxied through the host too, so range requests work and

artwork. Audio itself is
proxied through the host too, so range requests work and nothing is cached.

**The client half** is everything you see: the deck, the shelves, the drag and drop,
and a small sha
red store that keeps the sidebar and the panel in agreement.

## Tests
[代码示例省略，未执行]

There are no dependencies to install — the suites use only Node's standard
library. The offline ones

render the real components with a stub React and inspect
the result, which is how the deck's geomet

ry is verified: every disc is asserted to
be a `<circle>`, the cabinet is asserted to contain its pl

atter, and the tonearm's
stylus is asserted to land where it should. The browser probes cover what s

tatic
checks cannot see, such as how a real media element responds to a seek.
